Question: Let \(ABCDEF\) be an equiangular hexagon. The lines \(AB,\) \(CD,\) and \(EF\) determine a triangle with area \(192\sqrt{3},\) and the lines \(BC,\) \(DE,\) and \(FA\) determine a triangle with area \(324\sqrt{3}.\) The perimeter of hexagon \(ABCDEF\) can be expressed as \(m +n\sqrt{p},\) where \(m,\) \(n,\) and \(p\) are positive integers and \(p\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(m + n + p?\)
Solution:
An equiangular hexagon has interior angles \(120^\circ\). Extending alternate sides therefore makes two equilateral triangles, as in the figure: each small corner cut off by a hexagon side has angles \(60^\circ\).

[Figure 1](figures/2021_AMC_10A_Q21_official_solution_fig1.png)

Let \(x=BC+DE+FA\) and \(y=AB+CD+EF\). The hexagon's perimeter is \(x+y\). In the triangle formed by lines \(AB,CD,EF\), each of the three cut-off corners is equilateral. The three retained hexagon sides contribute \(y\) to this outer triangle's perimeter. A cut-off equilateral corner with hexagon side length \(s\) contributes its other two sides, totaling \(2s\). These three corner contributions total \(2x\), so the triangle's perimeter is \(y+2x\). The other triangle similarly has perimeter \(x+2y\).

For an equilateral triangle of side \(s\), the area is \(s^2\sqrt3/4\). The given areas yield side lengths
\[
\sqrt{4\cdot192}=16\sqrt3,
\qquad \sqrt{4\cdot324}=36.
\]
Their perimeters are \(48\sqrt3\) and \(108\). Adding the two perimeter equations gives
\[
3(x+y)=48\sqrt3+108,
\]
so the hexagon has perimeter \(36+16\sqrt3\). The requested sum is \(36+16+3=\boxed{55}\), choice C. Adding the two outer perimeters counts each hexagon side three times and avoids finding six separate lengths.
